title: Security & viruses
blurb: Viruses, scam pop-ups, firewall, encryption, safe browsing.

remedies.title: Turn on two-step sign-in (MFA) for my accounts
remedies.why: Two-step sign-in stops most account takeovers, even if a password leaks.

steps.text: Microsoft: account.microsoft.com/security › Advanced security options. Google: myaccount.google.com/security › 2-Step Verification. Apple: on by default.
Prefer an authenticator app or passkey over text messages.
Save the backup codes somewhere safe (not on the same computer only).

remedies.title: I keep getting sign-in approval requests I didn't start
remedies.why: Someone has your password and is hoping you'll approve by mistake.

steps.text: Deny every request you didn't start; never approve to make them stop.
Change your password now from a trusted device.
Report it as suspicious in the authenticator if offered.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT immediately for a work account.

remedies.title: Is this program or file safe to open?
remedies.why: You can scan a single file before opening it.

steps.text: Right-click the file › Scan with Microsoft Defender.
Unexpected attachments (even from people you know) can be malicious; check with the sender another way.
Never enable macros or "content" in a document you didn't expect.

remedies.escalate: Send suspicious work files to IT rather than opening them.

remedies.title: My files have strange names or a ransom note appeared
remedies.why: Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment.

steps.text: Disconnect from the network now (unplug the cable, turn off Wi-Fi). Don't turn the computer off.
Don't pay and don't contact the attackers.
Unplug backup drives so they aren't encrypted too.

remedies.escalate: Call IT immediately; on a work network this affects everyone.

remedies.title: Avoid showing private things when sharing my screen
remedies.why: Sharing the whole screen shows pop-ups, emails and other windows.

steps.text: Share one window instead of the whole screen.
Turn on Do not disturb / Focus while presenting.
Close private tabs and documents first.

remedies.title: "Memory integrity is off" or a driver is incompatible
remedies.why: Memory integrity blocks old drivers; one incompatible driver keeps it off.

steps.text: Windows Security › Device security › Core isolation details: see which driver is incompatible.
Update or uninstall the app that brought that driver, then turn memory integrity on and restart.

remedies.escalate: On work PCs, IT manages this setting.
